title: Conduct of Business and Suitability
summary: How to supervise firms' conduct of business arrangements, including client categorisation, disclosure, suitability and appropriateness assessments, and fair treatment of customers.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to supervise firms' conduct of business arrangements, including client categorisation, disclosure, suitability and appropriateness assessments, and fair treatment of customers.
Learning Objectives: Explain the core conduct of business obligations owed to clients
Assess suitability and appropriateness processes and file quality
Identify conduct risks arising from advice and distribution models
Syllabus: Client categorisation, disclosure and fair, clear and not misleading communications
Suitability and appropriateness: process, evidence and file reviews
Advice and distribution models and their conduct risks
Sample testing of client files: what good and poor look like
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors responsible for assessing firms' compliance and control arrangements
AML/CFT, conduct and governance specialists who review firms' policies, procedures and testing
Newer supervisors and staff moving into supervision from compliance roles in industry
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervision or of compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. Each masterclass is self-contained, so no prior attendance is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Compliance and the Compliance Function in Banks (2005)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
